text: How long can food sit on the counter? Two hours. And the reason is pure math.
Bacteria multiply by splitting in two, and in warm food they can do it every twenty minutes. One becomes two, then four, then eight.
In the fridge, they crawl. But between forty and one hundred forty degrees Fahrenheit, that's four to sixty Celsius, they race.
That's the danger zone, and your counter is right in it.
Cold doesn't kill bacteria. It only slows them down, and a freezer pauses them.
Two hours is six doublings: one becomes sixty four. Four hours, over four thousand. Eight hours, sixteen million.
And you can't see it, smell it, or taste it.
Reheating won't always save you. Some bacteria leave behind toxins that heat can't destroy.
So: two hours at most, one hour if it's hotter than ninety degrees. Keep the fridge at forty or below, and cool leftovers in shallow containers.
And thaw food in the fridge, never on the counter.
Watch again, and count the doublings.
